etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French dérivatif, from Latin dērīvātus, perfect passive participle of dērīvō (“to derive”). Related to derive; by surface analysis, derive +‎ -ative.
senses: Obtained by derivation; not radical, original, or fundamental.
Imitative of the work of someone else.
(linguistics) A word formed by derivation, such as stylish from style.
